title: Waste and recycling rates, targets and the Zero Waste Masterplan review
asked: Four MPs asked for figures on Singapore's waste and recycling — how much of the waste disposed of is recyclable, the split between industrial and domestic waste, and the main recycled categories — plus whether there is a yearly recycling target for 2026-2030, what measures are planned for glass, paper and textiles, whether the Masterplan review will focus on waste reduction or recycling rates, and how Singapore compares regionally and globally.
asked_by: Ms Poh Li San, Ms Valerie Lee, Ms Lee Hui Ying and Ms Hany Soh
response: Singapore disposed of 3.36 million tonnes of waste in 2025 — 1.67 million tonnes from domestic sources and 1.69 million tonnes from non-domestic sources — with a breakdown by waste type on the NEA website. Dr Janil Puthucheary said recycling rates are held down by three factors: a weaker business case for recyclers, stricter export requirements for recyclables, and contamination. He said MSE and NEA are reviewing the 2019 Zero Waste Masterplan, including its 70% recycling rate by 2030 target, and pointed to measures such as dedicated paper and cardboard collection since December 2025, additional blue bins at around 700 locations, and possible source-segregated bins.

key_points.point: Waste disposed of in 2025 was 3.36 million tonnes, split almost evenly between domestic (1.67 million tonnes) and non-domestic (1.69 million tonnes) sources.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: Singapore disposed of 3.36 million tonnes of waste in 2025, with 1.67 million tonnes from domestic sources and 1.69 million tonnes from non-domestic sources.

key_points.point: A breakdown of waste generated, disposed of and recycled by type is published on the NEA website.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: A breakdown by the type of the amounts of waste generated, disposed of and recycled can be found on the National Environment Agency (NEA) website.

key_points.point: One reason for lower recycling rates is that rising logistics, freight, manpower and energy costs have weakened the business case for recyclers.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: the business case for recycling has deteriorated due to rising logistics, freight, manpower and energy costs across the wider landscape

key_points.point: Receiving countries have tightened requirements for exported recyclables, and Singapore exports most of its recyclables.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: export markets for recyclables have become increasingly stringent in their requirements

key_points.point: Contamination of recyclables limits how much can be recovered and processed.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: the contamination of recyclables remains a persistent challenge, limiting the volume of recyclables that can be recovered and processed

key_points.point: International recycling-rate definitions differ, so cross-country comparisons are not always meaningful.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: Comparing recycling rates across countries is therefore not always meaningful if the bases are different.

key_points.point: The 2019 Masterplan set a 70% recycling rate by 2030 and a 30% cut in per-capita daily landfill waste by 2030; these targets will be reviewed for relevance.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: we had set a target of 70% recycling rate by 2030 and to reduce the waste sent to landfill per capita per day by 30% by 2030

key_points.point: Public Waste Collectors have added bins at around 700 locations and increased collection frequency at more than 1,100 locations.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: PWCs have deployed additional bins at around 700 locations and increased the collection frequency at more than 1,100 locations

key_points.point: Dedicated collection of paper and cardboard has been offered by all Public Waste Collectors in their zones since December 2025.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: NEA has also worked with all PWCs to offer dedicated collection of paper and cardboard in their respective zones since December 2025

key_points.point: Domestic waste generated per capita has fallen 21% over the past decade, and non-domestic waste per unit GDP by more than 30%.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: Domestic waste generated per capita has fallen by 21% over the past decade

key_points.point: Enhancing the National Recycling Programme could include source-segregated bins.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: This could include the use of source-segregated bins.

key_points.point: On the suggestion to adjust gate fees for industrial and commercial waste, the Ministry will consider looking at the fees.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: We will consider her suggestion on looking at the fees.

key_points.point: Blue bin contamination and public education will form part of the Zero Waste Masterplan review.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: It will certainly form an important part of the review of the Zero Waste Masterplan.

key_points.point: The review will consider whether to introduce new indicators or change the emphasis among indicators currently tracked.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: The study and the review will address whether we should introduce new indicators or whether we should change the emphasis between the indicators that we currently track, measure and target.

key_points.point: About half of Singapore's recycling material is exported and processed overseas under business arrangements with regional and overseas partners.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: about half of our recycling material is exported

left_open: The estimated proportion of the waste disposed of that is recyclable
The main categories of recycled waste and their corresponding proportions
An ideal yearly national recycling rate target for 2026 to 2030
Measures specific to glass and to textiles recycling
Data on recycling rates by region and globally, and how Singapore's rate compares with other countries
Whether nationwide clean-stream recycling bins will be implemented
supplementary: Supplementary questions covered shifting business behaviour through fees, blue bin contamination and public education, alternative progress indicators, upstream waste prevention, and regional recycling collaboration.
